newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: ROMANIA SEEN JOINING CEFTA NEXT YEAR - AIDE.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA SEEN JOINING CEFTA NEXT YEAR - AIDE.

text.p: Romania is expected to become the next member of the Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA) next year, a spokeswoman for Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said on Friday.

"The exact date has not yet been set, but it will be sometime during the course of next year," the spokeswoman, Magda Pospisilova, told journalists after Meciar's meeting with Romanian Prime Minister Nicolae Vacaroiu.
The two premiers met ahead of A summit of CEFTA prime ministers, which begins on Friday afternoon and is scheduled to discuss, among other issues, expanding the membership of the group.
Slovakia currently holds CEFTA's annually rotating chairmanship, which will pass on to Slovenia next year.
Romania would thus become the sixth member of CEFTA which now consists of the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Slovenia.

"The two prime ministers also discussed expansion of bilateral trade and possibilites of cooperation in the banking and financial sector," Pospisilova told journalists after the half-hour meeting of the two.
She added that both sides had expressed satisfaction that there were no political obstacles to deeper cooperation between the two countries.
Slovakia's imports from Romania in 1995 totalled $10 million and exports were $41 million.
The prime ministers of Bulgaria and Lithuania and the deputy premier of Ukraine and economics minister of Latvia are also attending tne summit as observers and potential members.
